structured.name: Montenegro
structured._source: wikidata (CC0); landBorders + naturalResources from CIA World Factbook (public domain)

prose.hook: Wedged between the Adriatic Sea and Serbia, Montenegro packs a highly indented coastline and rugged limestone mountains into a small footprint, giving it a strategic perch along the Adriatic. Its economy leans on bauxite deposits and hydroelectric power, with electricity, aluminum, and copper ore among its chief exports.
prose.physicalGeography: Montenegro sits in Southeastern Europe between the Adriatic Sea and Serbia. Its coastline is highly indented, backed by a narrow coastal plain that gives way quickly to rugged, high limestone mountains and plateaus.
prose.climate: The country has a Mediterranean climate along the coast, with hot, dry summers and autumns and relatively cold winters, while inland areas see heavy snowfalls. Destructive earthquakes are also a feature of the region.
prose.economy: Montenegro is an upper-middle-income economy, small even by Balkan standards, and uses the euro as its de facto currency despite not being part of the eurozone. Growth has slowed alongside a downturn in tourism and industrial production, though an energy price cap and falling food and services prices have helped ease inflation, and a new government has renewed momentum toward EU accession. Key industries include steelmaking, aluminum, agricultural processing, consumer goods, and tourism, with electricity, aluminum, copper ore, and packaged medicine among its leading exports.
prose.peopleAndCulture: Montenegrins make up 45% of the population, with Serbs at 28.7% and smaller Bosniak, Albanian, Muslim, Romani, and Croat communities. Orthodox Christianity is the dominant religion at 72.1%, followed by a significant Muslim minority at 19.1%, with smaller Catholic and atheist populations rounding out the mix.
